text:
alex.m: Heads up — started a small canary for per-tenant budgeted rollouts. Trying a new guard that stops traffic when a tenant's token-spend rate spikes above their budget-rate for >1m.
maria.s: Nice. Is that implemented as a hard pause or gradual throttle?
sam.k: It's a soft pause initially (traffic -> 0) with an alert; CLI/console can override. We also emit a telemetry event for why it paused.
tara: Can we avoid total zeroing? for chat flows a 0% kill is super disruptive. maybe route to a smaller cheaper model instead? :thinking_face:
kevin.p: +1 to fallback model approach. We already have compatible model variants; would prefer fallback to `redwood-small-v1` before pausing entirely.
maria.s: How does cost detection work? per-token per-tenant or sliding-window anomaly?
sam.k: Sliding window (30s, 1m, 5m). The guard has two checks: (1) sustained token rate > budget_rate * factor, (2) sudden per-request token spike (single request > token_threshold). Both configurable per-tenant.
alex.m: Example config snippet we discussed in design doc:
```
rollout_guards:
  tenant_budget_guard:
    enabled: true
    window_secs: 60
    factor: 1.5    # 150% of budgeted rate
    spike_threshold: 5000  # tokens in a single request
    action: fallback_or_pause
```
maria.s: Good. Need UX in console: show last triggered time, offending request id, and steps to unpause. Also show projected monthly burn delta if we let it continue.
sam.k: Telemetry emitted: `guard.triggered` with fields [tenant_id, guard_name, current_rate, budget_rate, offending_req_id, action_taken] — is that enough?
cost-ops-bot: FYI: ran a backtest on last month — for 120 tenants the sliding window caught 18 incidents, fallback would've saved ~32% of excess tokens vs full pause.
kevin.p: Any concerns about false positives for bursty workloads (e.g., embeddings batch jobs)?
tara: We should allow policy overrides: e.g., label tenant as `batch-exempt` or specify `burst_tolerance_secs`.
alex.m: Agree. Add a whitelist for scheduled batch jobs (by API key tag) and a tolerance parameter.
maria.s: How will rollout config look when applied to a canary A/B split? If 10% traffic to variant, guards should evaluate on absolute tenant slices, not global.
sam.k: Implementation note: guards evaluate per-tenant per-variant. So a tenant that hits spike under variant-a only affects variant-a's allocation for that tenant. Global routing still respects overall split.
kevin.p: That implies we need per-variant telemetry rollups. Console needs a heatmap: tenant x variant -> guard hits.
deploy-bot: canary:update 1815678901 started: variant-a 10% -> 10k req/min cap applied.
alex.m: Also add a hysteresis window: once paused, don't auto-resume for at least 5m unless manually cleared, to avoid flip-flopping.
tara: Make hysteresis configurable and surface in console with a countdown.
maria.s: UX: when user edits canary traffic (8% -> 20%), show a warning if tenant budgets could be exceeded and suggest fragmentation (stagger per-tenant ramp).
cost-ops-bot: Suggestion: add simulated "what-if" in console: if we increase variant to N%, show expected token burn per tenant based on last-7d profiles.
sam.k: Implementation caveat: computing what-if for thousands of tenants needs sampling or approximation; we'll add a batch job to precompute decayed moving averages.
kevin.p: Edge-case: long prompt conversations where tokens spike mid-request — spike_threshold shouldn't kill the whole tenant if the rest of requests are fine. Maybe flag the request and limit subsequent requests for 1m rather than pause variant entirely.
alex.m: Good point. We can chain actions: `flag_request -> throttle_key -> fallback_model -> pause_variant`. Each step emits telemetry.
maria.s: Also track false-positive rate and expose in console so customer success can tune.
tara: Are we defaulting to `fallback_or_pause`? need clear default order.
sam.k: Default action sequence: fallback_model -> throttle (reduce concurrency) -> pause_variant. We'll expose order as config and default to that.
deploy-bot: canary:event 1815678918 guard.triggered tenant=acme-corp guard=tenant_budget_guard action=fallback_model offending_req=req_8f3a
alex.m: Perfect. Please add a short paragraph in rollout UX spec about showing a replayable offending request (sanitized) + timeline. Maria can own the UI copy.
maria.s: I'll add it. Also want a toast-triggered CTA to contact support when a pause happens.
kevin.p: One more: logs must include kernel/model shard id in telemetry so infra can correlate with GPU memory pressure.
sam.k: Will include `model_shard` and `node_id` in telemetry.
alex.m: OK let's ship the guard as experiment flag in prod behind `budgeted_canary_v1`. Rollout plan: 1) enable for internal tenants, 2) 10% external tenants, 3) full. Monitor false positives and token-savings signal.
maria.s: Sounds good. I'll update the console mockups and add the what-if widget.
kevin.p: Thanks all.
